stem: of the five Ks that an initiated Sikh keeps, as listed in the Sikh Rehat Maryada, which one is the small wooden comb worn in the hair?
options: kara
kanga
kachera
kirpan
why: The Sikh Rehat Maryada names the five Ks of the Khalsa: kesh (uncut hair), kanga (a wooden comb), kara (a steel bracelet), kachera (a cotton undergarment) and kirpan (a sword). The kanga keeps the uncut hair clean and ordered.
source: Sikh Rehat Maryada, Amrit Sanskar section

es.stem: de las cinco K que guarda un sij iniciado, tal como las enumera el Sikh Rehat Maryada, ¿cuál es el pequeño peine de madera que se lleva en el cabello?
options: kara
kanga
kachera
kirpan
es.why: El Sikh Rehat Maryada nombra las cinco K del Khalsa: kesh (cabello sin cortar), kanga (un peine de madera), kara (un brazalete de acero), kachera (una prenda interior de algodón) y kirpan (una espada). La kanga mantiene limpio y ordenado el cabello sin cortar.

stem: which Guru gathered the hymns of the Gurus before him, added his own, and installed the first Sikh scripture, the Adi Granth, at the Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar in 1604?
options: Guru Angad
Guru Ram Das
Guru Arjan
Guru Hargobind
why: Guru Arjan, the fifth Guru, compiled the Adi Granth, with Bhai Gurdas as scribe, and installed it at the Harmandir Sahib in 1604. Guru Gobind Singh later added the hymns of Guru Tegh Bahadur and in 1708 named the scripture the Guru.

es.stem: ¿qué Guru reunió los himnos de los Gurus anteriores, añadió los suyos e instaló la primera escritura sij, el Adi Granth, en el Harmandir Sahib de Amritsar en 1604?
options: Guru Angad
Guru Ram Das
Guru Arjan
Guru Hargobind
es.why: Guru Arjan, el quinto Guru, compiló el Adi Granth, con Bhai Gurdas como escriba, y lo instaló en el Harmandir Sahib en 1604. Más tarde Guru Gobind Singh añadió los himnos de Guru Tegh Bahadur y en 1708 nombró Guru a la escritura.

stem: in the langar, the free kitchen of every gurdwara, people sit on the floor in rows called pangat and are served by volunteers. what is sitting in pangat mainly meant to teach?
options: that no one ranks above another, whatever their caste or wealth
that the eldest are seated nearest the Guru and served first
that the meal is karah prashad, the blessed food of worship
that sharing a meal earns merit toward a better next birth
why: Tradition traces the langar to Guru Nanak; Guru Angad and Guru Amar Das made it an institution, and Guru Amar Das is remembered for asking every visitor, even the emperor Akbar, to eat in pangat first. Sitting side by side on the floor, served the same food, sets aside caste and rank. Karah prashad is a separate offering given at the close of worship.
source: Sikh tradition on Guru Amar Das and the langar; Sikh Rehat Maryada, langar section

es.stem: en el langar, la cocina gratuita de cada gurdwara, la gente se sienta en el suelo en filas llamadas pangat y la sirven voluntarios. ¿qué busca enseñar sobre todo sentarse en pangat?
options: que nadie está por encima de otro, sea cual sea su casta o riqueza
que los mayores se sientan más cerca del Guru y se les sirve primero
que la comida es karah prashad, el alimento bendito del culto
que compartir una comida gana mérito para un mejor renacimiento
es.why: La tradición remonta el langar a Guru Nanak; Guru Angad y Guru Amar Das lo hicieron una institución, y se recuerda que Guru Amar Das pedía a todo visitante, incluso al emperador Akbar, comer primero en pangat. Sentarse lado a lado en el suelo y recibir la misma comida deja a un lado la casta y el rango. El karah prashad es una ofrenda aparte que se da al final del culto.

stem: the Guru Granth Sahib opens with Ik Onkar, written with the numeral one followed by the sign for Onkar. what does Ik Onkar affirm?
options: that Guru Nanak was the first of the ten Gurus
that the first hymn is sung before every other
that God stands apart from the world, far above it
that there is one God, one reality present in all
why: Ik Onkar, the first words of the Mool Mantar (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1), declares that the divine is one; the hymns go on to describe that one as present throughout creation.

es.stem: el Guru Granth Sahib se abre con Ik Onkar, escrito con el numeral uno seguido del signo de Onkar. ¿qué afirma Ik Onkar?
options: que Guru Nanak fue el primero de los diez Gurus
que el primer himno se canta antes que todos los demás
que Dios está apartado del mundo, muy por encima de él
que hay un solo Dios, una realidad presente en todo
es.why: Ik Onkar, las primeras palabras del Mool Mantar (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1), declara que lo divino es uno; los himnos siguen describiendo a ese uno como presente en toda la creación.

stem: Guru Hargobind, the sixth Guru, wore two swords, called miri and piri. what did the two swords stand for?
options: justice for the poor and mercy for the guilty
temporal authority and spiritual authority
his father's martyrdom and his own coming
the defense of Punjab and of the Harmandir
why: Guru Hargobind wore the swords of miri (worldly, temporal power) and piri (spiritual power) to show that a Sikh's life holds both together; the two curved swords of the Khanda are often read the same way.

es.stem: Guru Hargobind, el sexto Guru, llevaba dos espadas, llamadas miri y piri. ¿qué representaban las dos espadas?
options: justicia para los pobres y misericordia para los culpables
la autoridad temporal y la autoridad espiritual
el martirio de su padre y su propia llegada
la defensa del Punyab y la del Harmandir
es.why: Guru Hargobind llevaba las espadas de miri (el poder temporal, del mundo) y piri (el poder espiritual) para mostrar que la vida sij une ambas cosas; las dos espadas curvas del Khanda suelen leerse igual.

stem: a Sikh shopkeeper sets aside a tenth of what he earns (dasvandh) for the langar and for people in need. which of the three teachings often traced to Guru Nanak does this most directly carry out?
options: kirat karni, earning by honest labor
naam japna, remembering God's name
vand chakna, sharing one's earnings
chardi kala, keeping rising spirits
why: Vand chakna means sharing what you have earned before enjoying it; dasvandh, giving a tenth, is its best-known form. Kirat karni is the earning itself, and naam japna is remembrance of the name.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1245; Sikh Rehat Maryada

es.stem: un comerciante sij aparta la décima parte de lo que gana (dasvandh) para el langar y para quienes lo necesitan. ¿cuál de las tres enseñanzas que suelen atribuirse a Guru Nanak pone en práctica de forma más directa?
options: kirat karni, ganarse la vida con trabajo honrado
naam japna, recordar el nombre de Dios
vand chakna, compartir lo que se gana
chardi kala, mantener el ánimo en alto
es.why: Vand chakna significa compartir lo que uno ha ganado antes de disfrutarlo; el dasvandh, dar la décima parte, es su forma más conocida. Kirat karni es el ganar en sí, y naam japna es el recuerdo del nombre.

stem: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Guru, taught that a Sikh should be a sant sipahi, a "saint-soldier." what does each half of that ideal ask of a Sikh, and why are they held together?
why: Guru Gobind Singh, son of the martyred Guru Tegh Bahadur, founded the Khalsa in 1699 to join inner devotion with the courage to defend the oppressed, carrying forward Guru Hargobind's miri and piri.
source: Guru Gobind Singh; founding of the Khalsa, 1699

rubric.point: saint (sant): the inner life of devotion, remembering God's name, humility and self-control. "being religious" with nothing more specific is partly met.
soldier (sipahi): courage to stand up for justice and protect the weak or oppressed, not aggression or conquest. "fighting" alone, with no mention of protecting others or justice, does not count.

says why they go together: courage without devotion turns into mere violence, and devotion without courage can stand by while others suffer; or links the ideal to the Khalsa (1699), the kirpan, Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom, or miri and piri.

es.stem: Guru Gobind Singh, el décimo Guru, enseñó que un sij debe ser un sant sipahi, un "santo-soldado". ¿qué le pide al sij cada mitad de ese ideal, y por qué se mantienen juntas?
es.why: Guru Gobind Singh, hijo del mártir Guru Tegh Bahadur, fundó el Khalsa en 1699 para unir la devoción interior con el valor de defender a los oprimidos, continuando el miri y piri de Guru Hargobind.

stem: why do Sikhs treat the Guru Granth Sahib as their living Guru, and not only as a holy book?
why: In 1708, before his death, Guru Gobind Singh ended the line of human Gurus and passed the Guruship to the scripture. Sikhs hold that the Guru is present in the shabad, the Word, so the Guru Granth Sahib is honored like a living teacher: under a canopy, with a chaur, put to rest at night.
source: Guru Gobind Singh, 1708; Sikh Rehat Maryada

rubric.point: says Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Guru, ended the line of human Gurus (1708) and passed the Guruship to the scripture. saying only "the Gurus wrote it" does not count.
says the Guru is present in the words or teaching (the shabad, gurbani), so honoring it is honoring the Guru, not paper and ink.
mentions how it is treated as a living Guru (raised seat under a canopy, the chaur or whisk, put to rest at night, the daily hukamnama) or that Guru Arjan first compiled it (1604).

es.stem: ¿por qué los sijs tratan al Guru Granth Sahib como su Guru vivo, y no solo como un libro sagrado?
es.why: En 1708, antes de morir, Guru Gobind Singh puso fin a la línea de Gurus humanos y pasó la condición de Guru a la escritura. Los sijs sostienen que el Guru está presente en el shabad, la Palabra; por eso el Guru Granth Sahib se honra como a un maestro vivo: bajo un dosel, con un chaur, y se lo lleva a descansar de noche.
